items.headline: Tech Sector Leads Early Declines Amid AI Spending Concerns and Rising Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. equities opened lower on Thursday, primarily driven by a sharp retreat in technology stocks as renewed doubts concerning AI infrastructure spending resurfaced. This downward pressure was exacerbated by surging crude oil prices, which jumped above $111 a barrel due to escalating Middle East tensions, fueling inflation worries. The negative sentiment follows a positive close on Wednesday, where strong third-quarter earnings had provided a boost to the major indices.

items.headline: U.S. Economic Data Releases Point to Continued Growth
items.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau released new data from its Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) today, providing continuous, timely insights into business conditions. Separately, The Conference Board reported that its Leading Economic Index® (LEI) for the US was unchanged in September 2026, following a slight decline in August. The LEI's six-month growth rate showed a modest increase, suggesting the economy is still expanding, driven more by business investment than consumer spending. Real GDP growth is projected at 2.2% for 2026. Additionally, initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell to the lowest level since July.

items.headline: Oil Prices Jump Amid Escalating Middle East Tensions
items.summary: Brent crude surged past $111 a barrel on Thursday, reaching approximately $112, a near five-month high. This spike is attributed to renewed Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and reports of damage to oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, intensifying fears of supply disruptions and a broader conflict in the Middle East. The rise in oil prices has contributed to a risk-off sentiment in global equity markets.

items.headline: Tech Sector Retreats as AI Capex Fears Return
items.summary: The technology sector, particularly AI-linked companies, experienced a downturn on Thursday as investors expressed renewed doubts about artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.7% in early trading. This sentiment was partly fueled by Meta Platforms' ($META) report of negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012, despite beating revenue expectations, amid an 80% year-over-year increase in AI infrastructure spending. Tesla's ($TSLA) shares also fell post-earnings, with a cautious outlook on Optimus, delayed robotaxi revenue, and high chipmaking costs overshadowing an EPS beat.

items.headline: Key Company Earnings Reports Highlight Mixed Performance
items.summary: Several major companies released their third-quarter 2026 earnings today. Nasdaq, Inc. ($NDAQ) reported robust results, beating revenue expectations with $1.5 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.04, driven by a 17% increase in Solutions revenue. Lockheed Martin ($LMT) announced strong sales of $20.7 billion, up 11% year-over-year, and a record backlog of $292.0 billion. Procter & Gamble ($PG) advanced 6% after exceeding FQ1 expectations with 4% organic sales growth. Conversely, Blackstone ($BX) missed revenue estimates, and American Airlines Group Inc. ($AAL) reported a GAAP net loss of $269 million and forecasted another quarterly loss due to surging fuel costs, despite strong revenue growth. TTM Technologies ($TTMI) posted record net sales and non-GAAP net income, however, its stock was a top decliner today.
